problem:
Which of the following are logically equivalent to $A?$

- $¬B∧(A∨¬B)$
- $(¬B∨A)∧A$
- $A∧(¬B∨A)$
worked_solution:
The law that conjunction absorbs disjunction is stated as

$$
A∧(A∨¬B)≡A.
$$

With that in mind, let's inspect each of the given statements.

- Statement I is *not* logically equivalent to $A.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬B∧(A∨¬B) & ≡¬B∧(¬B∨A) \\  & ≡¬B≢A.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is logically equivalent to $A.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(¬B∨A)∧A & ≡A∧(¬B∨A) \\  & ≡A∧(A∨¬B) \\  & ≡A.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is logically equivalent to $A.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}A∧(¬B∨A) & ≡A∧(A∨¬B) \\  & ≡A.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
